analysis: The broad programme directly covers programming, systems, networks, databases, algorithm analysis, software development and visual computing. Advanced Algorithms and neural-network work add technical depth. Empirical design and product development contribute testing and user research rather than specialist computer science content.

The mathematical programme retains direct computing in programming, systems, algorithms, software construction and visual computing. Linear Systems, Advanced Calculus and Robotics add dynamic modelling, signal analysis and motion, and the AI sequence adds optimisation and learning. These focal applications make a substantive difference even with substantial common computing foundations.

Both develop numerical approaches to scientific problems. UvA teaches these methods through a dedicated project.

academicConstruction: Six original conflicts were resolved. In both options Image Processing & Computer Vision moves to term six and Optimization Methods in AI is offered there. Advanced Algorithms moves to term four in the broad option, with Research Methods & Statistics in the other vacated slot. In the mathematical option Robotics moves to term four and Software Development joins it. The broad option retains six advanced courses after replacing the generic ethics course with the moved optimisation course. The mathematical option retains six after dropping a neural-network course from the full final term. Four courses and 30 EC differ each way. The focus of the distinct group is application through robotics, signals and calculus versus advanced algorithms, practical neural networks and empirical evaluation, not only the numerical floor. A separate digital ethics or user-design direction has too little dedicated computing and repeats adjacent work already represented in both options.
